summary: Reveal now either lands on the item or is refused, and a refused reveal opens no window. ShellReveal.Walk asks the shell for the target once, through parse, then open-and-select, then free, passed in as delegates. It no longer climbs to an ancestor: RevealKind.Ancestor is deleted, and RevealPlan now carries a single Target. The status line says when a reveal was refused and that nothing was opened. The select-switch architecture rule is written in both ArchitectureRulesTests and fitness.yaml, and plant rows and xUnit Theories feed it every spelling it must catch and the look-alikes it must leave. Window case R-002 was built (steps a–e: deny-all folders, files at exactly 161/300/1000 characters timed from the hook's revealStartQpc, a pre-opened parent, and a deleted parent). R-001 was brought up to date: long-path matching, closing only its own windows, the refused dup. step, and step 10 at exactly 300 characters. Results: 496 of 496 Core tests pass, the rules harness has 68/68 rows as recorded, and R-002 step (e) passed through the published exe. The landing steps (R-002 a–d and R-001) were written but not run here, because they open Explorer windows that the case then has to close through Shell.Application.

files.why: Removed RevealKind.Ancestor and the climb. RevealPlan(Target, UnaddressableName, Requested) replaces the candidate chain. Walk(plan, requested, parse, open, free) tries the target once and refuses on any parse or open failure (NoLongerExists for 0x80070002/3; NameUnaddressable with 0x8007007B without asking the shell). The volume-root check for Hidden/System moved to IsRoot. Added internal wrappers ParseDisplayName, OpenFolderAndSelect and FreeIdList. Rewrote the class comment.

FormatRevealStatus now shows the refusal texts: NoLongerExists shows 'no longer exists ... Explorer was not opened. Rescan to refresh.'; any other failure shows "Couldn't show '<leaf>' in Explorer (<why>). Nothing was opened." The <why> is the Win32 message for FACILITY_WIN32 HRESULTs and the hex HRESULT for others. The catch path uses the same wording.

Replaced Walk_ItemDeleted_ClimbsToParent and the other climb tests with fake-shell tests: lands, not-found, other parse failure, open fails, unaddressable. Added Walk_OnRealTree_RefusesGoneTargetsAndLandsThePresentOne, which runs the real parse on an STA thread with a present file and a deny-all folder as controls. Plan tests now assert Target.
Feeds the rule's own pattern, read from ArchitectureRulesTests' source, the 5 launch spellings it must catch and the 3 look-alikes it must leave. It also pins which spellings SL-047's pattern missed.
New Fact NothingInTheAppHandsExplorerItsSelectSwitch over src/**/*.cs with the pattern /[Ss][Ee][Ll][Ee][Cc][Tt]\b.
Made FactPatterns and FindRepo internal so SelectSwitchRuleTests reuses them rather than keeping a third copy of the pattern reader.

Added the twinned entry 'NothingInTheAppHandsExplorerItsSelectSwitch (*.cs)' above the first settled marker, with (?m) and including_comments: true. Replaced the engine-appended settled copy of that rule with a comment, as SL-087 did. Kept the settled Ancestor rule.
Plants F31-F35 (must fire in both engines; F31/F32 also break SL-047's settled rule) and P25-P27 (must stay quiet). Updated the note's counts.

revealStartQpc and qpcFrequency on each reveal line, taken in a read-only class handler for PreviewExecuted of OpenInExplorer. Added FSA_HOOK_REVEAL_GATE, which holds the click after the scan until the case has changed the tree.

Added Initialize-RevealWin32 (GetLongPathNameW on \\?\ with a 32767-char buffer, EnumWindows, and a setup reveal). Added Get-ExplorerWindows and Find-Landing (resolved parent, exactly one selected item equal to the target). Rewrote Wait-ExplorerSelection. Added Close-CaseWindows (non-baseline windows under the case's own folders only), Get/Compare-ExplorerState and Watch-ExplorerUnchanged. Added Deny-All/Undo-DenyAll/Test-Listable, the stale-fixture sweep, Get-ExactPath, Invoke-WatchedReveal/Check-Landing/Invoke-RefusedReveal and the new case R-002 with -Step. R-001: scoped close, dup. now expects Failed with no window change, step 10 at exactly 300 characters. Registered R-002 in the ValidateSet, the hooked cases and All.
The design note: SL-047's fallback reversed, unaddressable names refused, Exact still taken from hr==0 (criterion 4), Hidden+System out of scope, and how each part is checked.

obligations.how: R-002 step (a) builds a short folder with a FullControl deny ACE for the current SID, applied through the .NET ACL API. Before the scan it checks that listing the folder throws UnauthorizedAccessException. It reveals the folder from its tree row and requires the parent's window with that folder as the only selection, matched by resolved path and also by Name. It also requires no new visible #32770 window owned by explorer.exe or the app, and no consent.exe, until 500 ms after landing. Written but not run here, because it opens an Explorer window the case must close. The Deny-All and listing check were exercised in a read-only probe (denied, then restored). The unit test Walk_OnRealTree_RefusesGoneTargetsAndLandsThePresentOne also shows the real parse reaching the open for a deny-all folder.

R-002 step (b): a file whose path is exactly 161 characters (checked with CheckEqual), 3 MiB, beside a sibling, revealed from its biggest-files row. It must land within 1000 ms of the hook's revealStartQpc, with both sides resolved through GetLongPathNameW. Written but not run here (it opens an Explorer window). The read-only probe confirmed the path builder and the matcher at 161 characters.

R-002 step (b): a 4 MiB file whose path is exactly 300 characters, revealed from its biggest-files row ('largest:'). It must land within 1000 ms and be the only selected item. The probe confirmed that the 8.3 form of a 300-character path resolves back and matches. R-001 step 10 is also padded to exactly 300 characters (tree row). Written but not run here (it opens Explorer windows).

R-002 step (d): a 5 MiB file whose path is exactly 1000 characters, created through .NET long-path calls, revealed from its biggest-files row. It must land within 1000 ms. The probe confirmed that GetLongPathNameW on the \\?\ form with a 32767 buffer turns the 183-character 8.3 alias back into the exact 1000-character path. Written but not run here.

R-002 step (c): a deny-all folder whose path is exactly 300 characters, denied through the .NET ACL API on its \\?\ form and checked as unlistable before the scan. It is revealed from its tree row and must land within 1000 ms as the only selection, with a Name check and the dialog/consent watch. Its target is different from the 300-character file's. The probe checked the deny and its undo. Written but not run here.

R-002 runs its steps in the order b, a, c, d, e. The 161-character reveal is therefore the run's first, with no warm-up, and is held to 1000 ms measured from the click (hook QPC) to the first matching read (pwsh QPC, taken after that read, so the figure errs long). Written but not run here.

R-002 step (d) first reveals the sibling through SHParseDisplayName + SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems from the case. It waits until Explorer is on the 1000-character file's parent with only the sibling selected, then reveals the file. Find-Landing looks at every ShellWindows entry and needs exactly one selected item equal to the target, and the case logs whether the landing reused the pre-opened window. Written but not run here.

Unit test: Walk_OnRealTree_RefusesGoneTargetsAndLandsThePresentOne deletes gone\ and runs the real parse on an STA thread. It asserts Failed/NoLongerExists with no open call, that the surviving parent parses S_OK, and that the present file and the deny-all folder do reach the open (passed). Window test: R-002 step (e) deletes gone\ after the scan through FSA_HOOK_REVEAL_GATE. It asserts Failed, NoLongerExists, the exact refusal text, and no Explorer window new, moved, re-selected or newly visible from launch until 2 s after exit. It ran through the published exe and PASSED.

The same real-tree unit test deletes kept\deleted.bin while kept\ remains. The real parse gives not-found, Walk reports Failed/NoLongerExists, and the open is never called (passed). The fake-shell Theory Walk_TargetNoLongerExists_RefusesWithoutOpeningAnything covers 0x80070002 and 0x80070003.

Walk_OpenFails_RefusesWithItsCodeFreesTheIdListAndTriesNothingElse: the fake parse returns S_OK with an ID list and the fake open returns E_FAIL. The test asserts Failed with E_FAIL, one parse, one open with that list, the list freed once, and Shown null (passed).

Walk_ParseFailsOtherwise_RefusesWithThatCode feeds 0x80070005, 0x8007007B, 0x80070035 and the non-Win32 0x80004005. Each must be Failed with that HRESULT, reason None (not NoLongerExists), and no open call (passed). The App's text for this branch falls back to hex for non-FACILITY_WIN32 codes (RevealFailure). That hex branch has no automated test, because there is no App test project. The other-failure text as a whole is asserted by R-001 step 3 (dup.), which was not run here.

SelectSwitchRuleTests.TheRuleCatchesEveryWayOfHandingExplorerTheSwitch feeds the Fact's own pattern ArgumentList.Add("/select"), "/SELECT," + p, "/select \"" + p, "/select," + p and the interpolated form (passed). It also pins that SL-047's pattern misses the first three. Harness plants F31-F35 in MainWindow.xaml.cs fire in both xUnit and Fitness: 8/8 AS-RECORDED, and 68/68 in the full run.

SelectSwitchRuleTests.TheRuleLeavesLookAlikesAlone checks "/selection", "selected" and "Open in Explorer" (passed). Plants P25-P27 stay quiet in both engines (AS-RECORDED). The clean harness baseline has 0 hits across src.

This is the real product run. The case published the app to artifacts/publish and built the hook. It made the R-002 tree: paths of exactly 161, 300 and 1000 characters, and both deny ACEs, verified as unlistable. It ran the shipped exe on it, deleted gone\ after the scan through the gate, and clicked Open in Explorer on victim.bin's tree row. Hook line: kind Failed, reason NoLongerExists, hresult 0x80070002, status "'victim.bin' no longer exists where the scan found it, so Explorer was not opened. Rescan to refresh.", revealStartQpc recorded. Explorer showed no new, moved, re-selected or newly visible window from launch until 2 s after exit. The fixture was deleted and its ACEs removed (checked afterwards).

tests.command: pwsh -File <temp probe>: the R-002 helpers loaded from WindowCases.ps1's AST, run read-only
tests.note: Opened no window. At 161, 300 and 1000 characters: the 8.3 alias (65/83/183 characters) resolves back to the exact path. Find-Landing matches the target alone, refuses a two-item selection and a different target, and matches an alias item by its resolved parent and name. Deny-All makes a folder unlistable and Undo-DenyAll restores it. Get-ExplorerWindows read the person's 1 open window, and a state compared with itself shows 0 changes. EnumWindows listed 306 top windows. The temp tree was removed.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case R-002 -Step a (and -Step b, -Step c, -Step d; and -Case R-001)
tests.note: Not run on purpose. Each opens real Explorer windows on the person's desktop. The case then has to Quit them through Shell.Application, and step (d) has Explorer pre-select a sibling. That is operating another program's windows, which this build may not do unattended. The close is now limited to non-baseline windows under the case's own tree, so a person or validate can run it without risk to their own windows. Whether the 1000 ms bound holds on a cold first reveal is therefore unmeasured by this build (the spikes' slowest was 934 ms).

deviations: A name the shell mis-parses (for example 'dup.', 'con', 'dir.\in.txt') is now refused: Failed, NameUnaddressable, 0x8007007B, and the shell is not asked at all. SL-047 used to open that name's parent with nothing selected. The design did not name this path, but deleting RevealKind.Ancestor removed that behaviour, and criterion 6 rules out opening another folder in the item's place. The design's 'rewrite any step expecting Ancestor to expect Failed with no window' covers R-001 step 3, which now asserts that. Plan returns RevealPlan(Target, UnaddressableName, Requested) instead of a candidate list, which is the design's 'cut down to the single target'.

TryReveal was not kept unchanged. The design also asked for an open-delegate seam, and the two cannot both hold. Walk now takes parse, open and free delegates, and RevealAsync passes internal wrappers of the same three shell32 calls in the same order: parse, open(pidl,0,NULL,0), then ILFree in a finally. The two public Walk overloads were replaced by one internal overload, which the tests reach through InternalsVisibleTo.

For a refused unaddressable name, the status text's (<why>) explains what Explorer cannot select, rather than showing a Win32 message. The rest follows the contract: Win32 message for FACILITY_WIN32 HRESULTs, hex otherwise, and the fixed NoLongerExists wording.

R-002 runs its steps in the order b, a, c, d, e. The design lists (a) first but also requires the 161-character reveal to be the run's first reveal with no warm-up, and only this order satisfies both.

Step (d) pre-opens the parent with the sibling selected through SHParseDisplayName + SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems, called from the case (a revealed sibling, as in the spike's case B), not through Shell.Application navigation. The case then checks with Find-Landing that Explorer shows only the sibling selected before the click.

Added a hook variable, FSA_HOOK_REVEAL_GATE. After the scan ends, the hook writes <gate>.ready and waits for <gate> before clicking. Step (e) needs gone\ deleted after the scan and before the reveal, and the hook had no seam for that. The hook only waits; the case does the delete.

The select-switch rule uses the pattern declared in the design's architecture_rules, /[Ss][Ee][Ll][Ee][Cc][Tt]\b, and not the component text's '(?mi)/select\b'. They match the same ASCII text. Explicit classes behave the same in .NET and in Python, and rules-parity's normaliser only strips a leading (?m). The engine-appended settled copy was replaced by the twinned entry plus a comment, following SL-087's precedent.

Find-Landing requires the resolved folder to equal the target's parent and exactly one selected item. That item matches if its resolved Path equals the target, or, when that Path does not resolve, if its resolved parent equals the parent and its Name equals the leaf. The fallback covers an item GetLongPathNameW cannot expand. Folder targets are also checked by Name, as designed.

WindowCases.ps1 gained a -Step parameter (a-e, comma-separated, R-002 only), so that each case key's command runs only its shape. FailCriticalErrorsTests.FactPatterns and FindRepo were made internal so that SelectSwitchRuleTests reads the rule's pattern from ArchitectureRulesTests' source without a third copy.
The real-tree unit test also includes a deny-all folder, which must parse and reach the recording open. The design asked only for the present sibling as a control.
not_built: Hidden+System targets (case C-014, not material): out of this slice as the design decided. The spike is waiting on a person, and the app still reports Exact with nothing selected for such items.
The product does not confirm a landing through Explorer's windows. As designed, Exact still comes from hr==0 and criterion 4 is held by the window tests. The open question to a person stands.
follow_ups: A person, or validate with permission to open and close Explorer windows, runs `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case R-002` and `-Case R-001`. That settles criteria 1, 2 and 5 and whether the cold first reveal lands within 1000 ms.
A follow-on slice for Hidden+System reveals, once the reveal-selects-hidden-and-system-items spike has run at Windows' default Explorer settings.

The App's refusal wording (FormatRevealStatus/RevealFailure) is checked only through the window cases. Its non-FACILITY_WIN32 hex branch has no automated test. It could move into a Core formatter with a unit test if a person wants that branch pinned.
The design's open question on criterion 4 (should the app confirm the landing in Explorer before reporting success) still needs a person's answer.

architecture.find: and 'open in Explorer' (explorer /select or SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems) on any item.
architecture.replace: and 'open in Explorer' on any item, through SHParseDisplayName and SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems only (never Explorer's select switch), which opens the item's parent with the item selected or, when that cannot land, says so on the status line and opens nothing.
architecture.why: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/ShellReveal.cs Walk: one parse, then open, refused on any failure; RevealKind is Exact|Failed. src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs FormatRevealStatus: the refusal texts. ArchitectureRulesTests.NothingInTheAppHandsExplorerItsSelectSwitch and its fitness.yaml twin forbid /select anywhere in src; rules-parity AGREE and harness F31-F35 fire. R-002 -Step e through the published exe showed Failed/NoLongerExists and no Explorer window.
